capture_source: live capture 2026-08-28, contributed via issue #29; SAP S/4HANA 2023 kernel 793 release 758, unicode. RFC_READ_TABLE on OA2C_CLIENT with USE_ET_DATA_4_RETURN='X'. Sanitised: GW handle and 0x0514 session token overwritten, and every column value inside <LINE> replaced with 'X' of the SAME length so the delimiter structure and all field widths are preserved. No NI length prefix.
evidence: decodes to one row of five pipe-delimited columns matching the four requested FIELDS plus the client UUID
notes: USE_ET_DATA_4_RETURN='X' makes the server return rows through ET_DATA in BASXML instead of the binary DATA table - which comes back declared (0x0301/0x0330/0x0302) but with NO rows.
BASXML shape: an empty 0x3c02 brackets the block on both sides, with the XML split across 0x3c05 records. The payload is ASCII, NOT the UTF-16LE every other string-bearing tag uses.

The fragments are one XML document split at arbitrary points: here chunk 1 is '<ET_DATA>' and chunk 2 is '<item><LINE>...</LINE></item></ET_DATA>'. Only the first fragment names the table - a later one may begin '<item>' - so the name must be taken once on entry, not re-derived per chunk.

The row form observed is the shortcut one: a single <LINE> element holding the whole delimited row, exactly the buffer DATA would have carried. The documented alternative puts one element per field; both are handled by the same walk, since whatever elements an <item> contains become that row's keys.

[ASSUMED] Multi-row behaviour. This capture has a single <item>, so how several rows are distributed across 0x3c05 fragments is inferred from the fact that the fragments form one document. Joining before parsing makes the split irrelevant, but a multi-row capture would confirm it.
